title: Drums of March
subtitle: The opening notes of a big crescendo.

trails.title: Suggestion Box
trails.description: An effective way for interdepartmental communication and understanding the needs of all employees.

content.text:
Title: Feedback on "Faces"

Submitter: ■■

Content: Who thought the Michael and Jason horror masks were a good idea? And what's with the creepy face of the little tank engine? Enough already, my heart can't take this!

Collection Point: Laplace ■■ Department, First Floor.

Collection Date: ■/28

Reply Received on ■/30: This plan was recommended anonymously with the intention of using familiar characters to create a sense of closeness among employees. However, these masks failed to achieve the desired effect. Mask Plan Mark II has now been initiated.

——————————

Title: Fourth Floor, Keep an Eye on Your Test Animals!

Submitter: Tom Evans

Content: Stop letting your spiders run wild—they've already eaten six of our Madagascar hissing cockroaches! This is seriously affecting our progress! These are crucial pieces of experimental data and research that are at stake here!

Collection Point: Laplace Headquarters, Fourth Floor.

Collection Date: ■/3

Reply Received on ■/30: Look, just because we're researching the Spider Tail doesn't mean we're responsible for any of this. Our Spider Tails don't even contain actual spider parts! Maybe you should ask the third floor instead, they're the ones studying the hydraulic legs.

——————————

Title: Sincere Advice for Madam Lucy
Submitter: A person with a single letter for his name.

Content: Given that Madam Lucy is an incredibly sophisticated computer with no emotional modules, and I am a carbon-based life form naturally equipped with such modules, I would like to make some modest suggestions. It could be beneficial for Madam Lucy to learn more about interacting with our carbon-based employees. This includes not entering their offices without prior notice, developing a better sense of humor, and not removing important components from their delicate machinery.

Collection Point: Laplace Headquarters, next to the Director's office.

Collection Date: ■/■

Reply Received on ■/31: Hello, X. The set of devices you designed is unnecessarily complicated—the work it is doing far exceeds the joules needed to brew a pot of coffee under normal conditions, so I made some adjustments. As for your other points, I noticed today that my office wall is now covered with fake 230V sockets. Is this what you call a sense of humor?

items.text: Drums of March
Laplace Main Hall

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Move, ugh, move!
Navigating this corridor is no easy feat, as researchers, engrossed in their Brownian motion studies, hurry along without watching their step.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: ... Shoot, are you blind, or did you hit me on purpose?
A viscous, deep purple substance drips from their face onto the hem of their lab coat, marvelously landing in a spot not yet coated with other stains.

items.speaker: Laplace Staff I
items.text: Hey! Hello!

items.speaker: Laplace Staff I
items.text: Do you know how to control this thing?

items.speaker: Laplace Staff I
items.text: It always drips on my bread at lunch. I had to skip breakfast for a week.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Just remove your brain. Problem solved.

items.speaker: Laplace Staff I
items.text: That makes sense. How come I didn't think of that? Thank you for your advice. You are so sweet.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Oh, you're so welcome, pal.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: I'd wipe my eyes more often if I were you. Just do something to get that black snot off those lashes.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: The good news is, the persons in charge of this place are all dead ...

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: The bad news, the one in charge right now is not a "person"!
"Storm" Observation Room

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Hello, Researcher Medicine Pocket. Your meal allowance is being deducted to pay for door repair.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text:
I don't care, bucket head.
Do your worst, a few pennies don't bother me.
The head of the computing center nods, taking this as a sign of amicable agreement.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: You could have called me from your lab terminal. The technology department has equipped every researcher with the latest communication device, and I have the energy to communicate with everyone.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Then how am I supposed to know whether my report is lying in your trash or not? Oh please, you know we gotta talk face to face to solve our issues when things get ugly.
With a flick of their wrist, a gray folder lands with impact, spilling its contents across the desk.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Congrats on the one and only achievement you got from the Manus Mask: we're now fully aware of its side effects! And this great achievement is filling the halls with oil and insanity!

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: You should thank the hatted cuckoo for her report. No one's turned into a crazy monster yet, or the Manus would be attacking the headquarters from Laplace right now!

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: D**n it, what are you doing? Are you even listening to me?!
Lucy turns her head, having just fastened the buckle on her face.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: My apologies. You said we needed to talk "face to face."

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: If I understand it correctly, this is your number one request.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: ... You always carry a face in your pocket? That's just ... great.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: You are welcome. It is our duty to learn and meet the needs of every researcher. This will help them reach their full potential while respecting the nature of their being.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I received some letters of complaint. They asked me to develop a better sense of humor. They said it would help me understand the researchers' sarcasm, so I am studying it.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: 75% of the complaints mentioned they did not want to see a face on my head. Some even used strong words like "Never let me see that face of yours again!"

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I am glad that you are one of the other 25%, Researcher Medicine Pocket.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: You know what, I don't mind if you keep that face on, as long as you let me kick it around a bit.
The newly face-flaunting robot nods slightly, pleased with their renewed consensus.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Regarding your second request, I have read your report. I fully understand the side effects of the mask as well as the ... feasibility of the decryption.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Then what's the point? It's like trying to get the syrup formula out of a coke can! Ugh! Again, we are all screwed without the original ritual from the Manus!

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: It is too early to conclude that the mask does not contain important clues. The attempts we are making are very necessary.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Besides, the situation in Laplace is not as bad as you say. The side effects are completely under control. The subjects are only suffering from dehydration and mania.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Fortunately, the Rehabilitation Center has extensive experience in dealing with manic patients. And some researchers, like yourself, are already manic without putting on the mask, so the side effects will not affect them much.

items.speaker: Laplace Staff I
items.text: Hahahaha! Yes! Ball pens! Ball pens love brains!
Two researchers arrive swiftly, removing the poor soul who lodged a pen into their eye socket and just as swiftly replacing the broken glass.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Extensive experience, huh?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: That is right. I am glad you have noticed our efforts. We have prepared a large amount of polymer materials in case of minor vandalism by the patients.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Hahaha, amusing.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: So this is the logic of a machine, huh? Humans are as expendable in the lab as glass. You should be glad that your head is harder than my teeth, or I'd ...

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Your opinion surprises me, Researcher Medicine Pocket. There is a big difference between the human body and glass.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: As for the original ritual, you are not the first researcher to make this suggestion. We are fully aware of its importance.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: We have dispatched investigators and members of the Field Agent Administration to investigate various regions. Here are the images they sent back.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Field ... What?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Field Agent Administration. If you have not heard of the name before, most prefer to call them the History Guards, given their function.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Right. That team of cannon fodder.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: The thought of people being thrown around like garbage makes me feel lucky ... that I'm just a piece of glass.
Medicine Pocket lifts their head, examining the screen. Their attention completely diverted.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Looks like "face to face" conversation does solve problems. Finally we're getting somewhere, aside from the insane colleagues running amok.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Let me guess. The blue dots are good news, huh?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Correct. They represent the safe areas immune to the "Storm."

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Ahh, North America ... I should've gone there for a walk in the park. I don't deserve to suffer in this stupid gray prison.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I have to say, Researcher Medicine Pocket, even though I approved your request for a sports field, which you claimed was a humanitarian need, I think it is more of a canine need.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: I suggest you install an indicator on your humor module, so we know when to laugh. See, like this blinking red dot ...

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Hm, is that Vienna?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Yes.
They wait, but the android does not offer up any further information.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text:
Alright, alright. "Not privy to the information," huh? I know of your tricks.
One day I will find the logical fallacies in your words, I swear.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: And, this here ...

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Yellow. Better than the worst, worse than the best.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: That's the Aegean Sea. What's all the fuss about? Don't tell me there's a five hundred meter long blue crab ...

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: No. No sightings of large marine organisms other than the Gorgon.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: This is where Timekeeper and her team are right now.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: By the way, it seems you can distinguish between colors precisely, so the canine elements in you are more of a personal choice than an innate trait.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: I see your efforts on improving your sense of humor, I do, but that's enough now. Turn off the module, ok? Who the heck put these complaints in the box?! I'm gonna kick their teeth out!

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Back to business. Timekeeper and her team are in a bit of a situation. The details are classified, and I am not privy to them either.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Hah, "classified." I know what's going on. In this place, "classified" means ...

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: They're in big trouble!

items.speaker: Pilot
items.text: D**n it! What are they?!

items.speaker: Pilot
items.text: Krupp did not tell us about these things!

items.speaker: Pilot
items.text: D**n it! Get away from me, you arcane fiends!
Marcus?
Ooh!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I'm sorry, Madam Hofmann. I was reading the newspaper ...!

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I know I told you to practice your arcane skills more, but you don't have to do it all the time.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I just told you the oath to secrecy for this mission. Level Two Investigator Marcus, repeat it to me.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Uhm ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Remember the Field Mission Manual ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Never disclose any information about the "Storm" or the "era" to irrelevant people.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Never build unnecessary connections with the current era. Never disclose any real information about the headquarters to members of the branch. Never discuss confidential matters in unrelated settings.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Never contact or interfere with the insignificant. Stay out of their lives, silently observe and respect their lives ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: And, why is the stupid train never on time?

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Did I really say that?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Yes, in a low voice, after the last random stop.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: You have a talent for multitasking, I'll give you that. But the point is, as a rookie investigator, your focus should really be on the mission.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Y-Yes, Madam Hofmann. I'm so sorry ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Laplace has analyzed the information from the Field Agent Squad and suggested several Critical Points on where the "Storm" may arrive. One of them is Vienna.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The History Guards have reported sightings of Manus leaders there. Considering they will probably do the same thing they did in 1929, you know, escalate international conflicts to accelerate the reverse, this mission is probably quite risky.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: It's okay, Madam Hofmann. I am fully prepared!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I've been waiting for my first field mission since I joined the Foundation. Thank you for approving my application, or I'd still be talking to rusty filing cabinets and diamond patterns on a wall ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: No need to thank me, Investigator Marcus. Your application has been approved by headquarters, as your arcane skills will prove very useful on this mission.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: This time we will track down Manus Vindictae in Vienna and gather intelligence on their rituals. The intelligence should help with the "Storm" immunity research, making it the top priority over all other missions.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: That's why I said your arcane skill, "reading," will be useful on this mission.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Yes ... Understood!
The young student straightens up. Her mentor catches her emotion and replies unsmilingly.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I know how lucky you must feel for returning to your era, after being isolated from the outside world for so long.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I will take you to Romania and visit the orphanage where you used to live, if we still have time for that after the mission.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I'll do my best, Madam Hofmann! Whatever you need, as long as my arcane skill can do it!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: By the way, how's the Timekeeper doing on that Aegean island?

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Marcus, have you already forgotten what I just told you?! This is a confidential matter!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But it's in the news.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Unknown island appears on the Aegean Sea. Forces attacked by arcane creatures."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Ownership over island causing conflicts between Bulgaria, Serbia, and Greece."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Austro-Hungarian Empire and Russian Empire to establish a negotiating committee ..."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Madam Hofmann, the increased turmoil could cause the "Storm" to arrive earlier, right?

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: That is not our problem. The headquarters will send someone to intervene, since it is caused by the arcanum.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Now just focus on our destination, Vienna.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Time to get out. Grab your luggage.
TO BE CONTINUED…
